listing.name: Doom 3: Resurrection of Evil (classic) (dhewm3)
listing.summary: Set up Doom 3: Resurrection of Evil (classic) through its upstream dhewm3 player using your own original files. Setup, profiles and updates stay upstream-owned.

steps.title: Use this original game and edition
steps.instruction: Use classic Doom 3 patched to 1.3.1 base/pak000.pk4 through pak008.pk4 plus your Resurrection of Evil d3xp/pak000.pk4 and pak001.pk4. Expansion files alone and BFG Edition do not provide this route. Keep your originals elsewhere unchanged; upstream handles its own data recognition and preparation. A Portcove registration does not authenticate original-game files.

steps.title: Prepare upstream and select the real player
steps.instruction: Use the main official dhewm3 1.x Windows win32 ZIP, retaining its DLLs and resources. This is the reviewed 32-bit Windows player, not an x64 artifact; the existing Windows registration route supports PE32. The separate dhewm3-mods archive supplies optional mod libraries. Register dhewm3.exe inside its wrapper with that same folder as working directory, not the dedicated server or a helper. Put original data in the matching base/d3xp folders or pass three separate argument lines, +set, fs_basepath, then the absolute folder containing them. To select Resurrection of Evil, add three more argument lines: +set, fs_game, d3xp.

steps.title: Keep the actual original and player data
steps.instruction: Windows normally uses the actual Documents/My Games/dhewm3 profile for configuration, saves, screenshots and logs, with separate base and d3xp game directories. Explicit fs_savepath and other original/mod paths can redirect storage. Preserve all actual locations and the working runtime with the game closed before replacing upstream files. The original game, expansion, demo and BFG Edition remain different data scopes; mods needing game DLLs require their own compatible dhewm3 build.

steps.title: Keep external ownership and deliberate Play
steps.instruction: Finish upstream setup first. Registration saves your selected executable, working directory and literal arguments; Play is a separate explicit action. You and upstream own this external runtime, original files and profile. Registration-only removal preserves them. Managed Update, Backup, Rollback, migration and deletion are not offered for these external files. Preserve a working copy and its data before upstream replacement. Other platforms require their own supported upstream application/native flow.
